title: Silent data loss on a failed save — UI disables Save identically on HTTP 500 and 2xx with no error feedback
stepsToReproduce: Open Terms and Conditions for office 1604 with US English filter.
Make a valid edit (e.g. change a row's language).
Click Save when the server returns a non-2xx response (observed: HTTP 500).
Observe: Save button transitions to disabled, no toast, no banner, no inline error message, no console error surfaced to the user.
expectedBehavior: On a non-2xx save response, the UI should signal an error (toast, banner, or inline message) and keep Save enabled so the user can retry or take corrective action.
actualBehavior: On one observed HTTP 500, the UI disabled the Save button exactly as on a successful 2xx response. No toast, no banner, no inline message, no console error was surfaced. The user receives no indication that their data was not saved. Corroborating incident: a later run's cleanup save failed this way and left row AUTOMATION-TEST-ROW-TNC-WALKX wrongly named on the server — the bug caught the tester.
mcpEvidence: Live-verified 2026-08-06 by tnc-persistence-r1 (HTTP 500 exchange observed) and probe9 (UI-behaviour observation across all trials: button disables post-save regardless of outcome, zero alerts/toasts/console errors). Evidence: out-probe9/PROBE9.md §JOB2, out-walk-salvage/WALKR2.md §Job 1 (restore failure showing WALKX name persisted).
baselineEvidence: Old site uses per-cell inline saves with immediate visual feedback. The bulk-save-with-no-error-feedback pattern is new-site-only.
